_comment: Prompt-cache lifetime. Merge the two keys below into the host repo's .claude/settings.json; removing them undoes it. Each takes "5m" or "1h". promptCacheTtl covers the main conversation (interactive, -p and SDK turns); left unset, Claude Code picks 1 hour on a Claude subscription within its usage limits and 5 minutes on an API key, Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry. subagentPromptCacheTtl covers everything outside the main conversation (subagents, workflows, background and helper requests); left unset, it is 5 minutes. WHY 1h: a Builder or QA run that waits on a test suite for longer than the lifetime finds its cache gone, and the next turn pays full input price for the whole session. THE TRADE-OFF: a 1-hour cache write is billed at a higher rate than a 5-minute one (2x base input against 1.25x at the time of writing, the figures in the plugin's issue 57), so a repo whose runs never pause for more than 5 minutes pays more with these keys, not less. The env vars CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL win over these keys, and these keys win over an agent's frontmatter. Issue 57 reports that Claude Code 2.1.318 or newer reads them. Not checked by the plugin: that every Claude Code version reads the two keys from a project's settings file, and what the Actions lanes (claude-code-action) do with them.
